1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to so that each participant who uses a gets safe support that fits them and their own machine. It is for participants, their families and advocates, our workers, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Everyone who works for [Provider name]: employees, contractors, agency workers, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every participant for whom a worker starts, fits, checks, cleans or answers a ventilator. This includes a ventilator used through a mask and one used through a . It includes bilevel and CPAP machines where the says the participant depends on the device or cannot manage it without a worker. Otherwise, help with a CPAP or bilevel machine is ordinary personal care under the participant's .
  • Every setting: the participant's home, a shared home, a day program, a vehicle and the community.

A ventilator that the participant sets up and uses entirely alone is outside this policy, unless their plan says workers must help.

3Commitments

C1

We will start ventilator support only under a written plan and prescription from the participant's treating team. We start only after the in FRM-HID-10 is complete and signed. We never write, fill a gap in or change the plan.

C14

We will use standard infection precautions for every circuit, mask, humidifier and suction task. Single-use parts are used once, parts are cleaned or changed on the dates the plan and the supplier set, and suction waste and used protective equipment are disposed of safely.

C15

We will keep a training plan for each participant who uses a ventilator. It names every worker, the training each needs, the and the date it is due.

4Ground rules

G1

No one at [Provider name] sets or changes a value the treating team has prescribed: a mode, a setting, an alarm limit, an oxygen flow or the hours of use. A signed-off worker turns prescribed oxygen on and off at the prescribed flow, and adjusts a comfort setting, only where the sheet says so.

G2

No alarm is disabled, muted or turned below the volume the plan sets. A worker pauses an alarm only after the cause is fixed, only with the control the supplier's instructions give, and never leaves the participant while an alarm is paused. A participant is never left on a ventilator with the alarm silent.

G3

A worker never holds a participant, and never fits a device that is not in the plan, to stop them removing a mask or a tube. A device the treating team prescribes for a clinical purpose is used only as the plan says. The and a behaviour support practitioner decide before first use whether it is a under POL-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Policy. A hold or a device used to influence behaviour is a regulated restrictive practice and, without authorisation, a reportable incident.

G4

A participant's choice to be off the ventilator, or to refuse a task, is respected. We explain the risk, tell the treating team the same day and record it on FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record. We never force.

G5

There is one plan: the treating team's. Where the participant also has a tracheostomy, POL-HID-05 Tracheostomy Management Policy and PRO-HID-04 Tracheostomy Management Procedure add rules. They do not add a second plan.

G6

The equipment belongs to the participant, the treating team or the supplier. We never open or repair a ventilator or a battery, and we never lend equipment. A signed-off worker swaps external batteries, circuits, filters and humidifier chambers as the sheet and the supplier's instructions say. Only the supplier replaces a machine or an internal battery. We never use one participant's parts for another.

G7

Only a signed-off worker does a ventilator task. A sign-off for one participant, one machine or one task does not carry over to another.

G8

We offer ventilator support only while ventilator management is on our certificate of registration (Practice Standards Rules, section 13C).

G9

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead, and cannot sign off their own competency. They engage a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers the support, for both, and they need a second signed-off person before taking on the participant. They name an independent contact for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

G10

Ventilator records are health information. We share them only with the participant's consent, or where the law requires or allows it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy applies.

G11

A family member who runs the participant's ventilator does so under the treating team's training. We do not direct them, and we do not ask them to do our tasks.

G12

Nobody is penalised for raising a concern about ventilator safety or staffing. Reports follow POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy.

418 words
ventilator
a machine that moves air into and out of a person's lungs, through a mask or through a tracheostomy. It includes bilevel and CPAP machines when workers help with them.
treating team
the respiratory doctor, home ventilation service or other health practitioners who prescribe the participant's ventilator and write or endorse their plan.
plan
the treating team's written plan and prescription for this participant. It may sit in FRM-HID-01 Participant Health Support Plan if the team has written or endorsed it there.
signed-off worker
a worker whom the trainer has signed off, task by task, for this participant and this ventilator, and whose sign-off is current.
trainer
a health practitioner, or a person who meets the NDIS Commission skills descriptor for ventilator support, who trains and signs off workers.
Clinical Lead
a registered nurse, or another health practitioner whose scope covers the support, whom [Provider name] engages to oversee high intensity supports. A sole trader cannot be their own Clinical Lead and engages one.
alarm
a sound or message on the ventilator that tells a worker something is wrong.
readiness check
the questions in Section D of FRM-HID-10. Every answer must be yes before the first shift.
advance care directive
a document in which a person sets out the care they do or do not want if they cannot say so themselves.
own oxygen level
how much oxygen is in the participant's blood, usually measured with a probe on the finger. It is not the oxygen the ventilator delivers.
regulated restrictive practice
a restrictive practice the NDIS rules regulate, such as physical restraint or mechanical restraint.
manual ventilation
moving air into the lungs by hand, with a resuscitation bag joined to the mask or the tracheostomy.
move-by time
how long before a battery runs out the participant must be on other power or moved. The treating team sets it.
life support customer
a customer registered with an electricity retailer and distributor because someone at the address depends on life support equipment.
tracheostomy
an opening in the neck, with a tube in it, through which a person breathes.
incident
has the meaning in POL-INC-01 Incident Management Policy.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
on-call manager
the manager who takes workers' calls. In office hours this is the Service Manager. After hours it is the rostered manager. A clinical question goes to the treating team's clinical number, or to the Clinical Lead.

1Purpose

The result: a participant who uses a has a made with them and prescribed by their . Workers are trained and signed off on their own machine. A safe response is ready for an , a failure or a power cut, at any hour.

This procedure gives effect to POL-HID-07 Ventilator Management Policy, C1 to C15.

2When and who

Start this procedure:

  • when a participant who uses a ventilator asks for our support, at step 1
  • at the start of every shift with that participant, at step 10
  • the moment an alarm sounds, the power fails or the participant is in trouble, at step 19
  • every week, every month and at each review, at step 27.

Ventilator management means supporting a participant to use a machine that moves air into and out of their lungs, through a mask or through a . It includes the machine, its alarms and power, the mask or tube, the humidifier, oxygen if prescribed, suction and . It covers bilevel and CPAP machines when workers do ventilator tasks for the participant.

Where the participant also has a tracheostomy, PRO-HID-04 Tracheostomy Management Procedure applies as well. There is still one plan.

In this procedure, the bag means the manual ventilation (resuscitation) bag with the mask or adapter the sheet names. A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

  • The Service Manager asks the participant, gets the plan, sets the staffing rule, arranges the health review, runs the , checks every record for completeness each week and runs the monthly equipment test. In office hours the Service Manager is also the .

4Watch out

  • A ventilator that stops can harm a participant within minutes. Stay with them and call 000. Ventilate by hand if you are signed off. Phone a manager second.
  • Never change a prescribed setting, mode, alarm limit or oxygen flow. A wrong setting can fail to ventilate the participant or harm their lungs. Only the treating team changes them. Turn prescribed oxygen on and off, and adjust a comfort setting, only where the sheet says so.
  • Never disable or mute an alarm, and never turn it below the volume the plan sets. Pause one only after the cause is fixed, with the supplier's control, and never leave the participant while it is paused. If you cannot hear it, you cannot answer it. An alarm that stops by itself still needs checking and writing down.
  • Be awake and within hearing. A worker who is asleep, in another building or wearing headphones gives no protection. The staffing rule says who must be awake.
  • A battery runs out, and a registration does not stop a power cut. Know the before you need it. Life support registration gives notice of planned outages only.
  • A generator can kill. Its fumes are poisonous. Run it outside only. Never run it in a home, a garage or a vehicle.
  • Oxygen feeds a fire. Keep it away from flames, heaters and smoking. Use only the flow the team prescribed. The oxygen the machine delivers is not the participant's . Never mix the two up.
  • Vomit under a mask can block the airway. Take the mask off at once if the participant is sick or about to be, unless the sheet gives other steps.
  • Never hold or restrain a participant, and never fit a device that is not in the plan, to keep a mask or tube on. It can be a , and a reportable incident. A device the treating team prescribes is used only as the plan says, after the Clinical Lead and a behaviour support practitioner have decided what it is. Stay, reassure and phone the treating team.
  • Never use another person's equipment, or do a task you are not signed off for. The wrong mask or the wrong setting can harm. A sign-off for one participant, one machine or one task does not carry over.
  • Skin under a mask can break down. Look at it every time the mask is off. Tell the Clinical Lead about any sore.

Service Manager, every week: check each completed FRM-HID-10 for blanks, a missed check, a no at the hearing question and a missed due date, and phone the worker about each gap. Clinical Lead, every month: read a sample of the participant's records, and every record after an incident or a plan change. Look for a mismatch, an alarm pattern and a power cut. Enter each action in REG-QMS-01 with an owner and a date. Send the treating team the alarm and observation pattern, with the participant's consent. Every 3 months, count mismatches, alarms, power cuts and missed checks for the Quality Manager's trend report to the governing body. Every 12 months, ask each participant and their workers what would make the support safer, and record what changes.

Result
Gaps in completeness are found within a week, clinical patterns within a month, and each has an owner and a date.
Record
FRM-HID-10 Q68. REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register
Time limit
Every week for completeness, within 7 days of the last entry. Every month for the sample, and after every incident or plan change. Trend counts every 3 months. System review every 12 months (our standard)

Step 28

Warning. A backup that has never been tested is a hope, not a backup.

The Service Manager, or a senior signed-off worker the Service Manager names. The Clinical Lead reviews the result

Run the monthly equipment check.

Test the backup ventilator, the batteries and any generator with the supplier's checklist and as the supplier's instructions say. Check each service date on the sheet and chase any that are overdue. Check the stock of spare parts and consumables, and ask the supplier to send any that are short. We never service a ventilator ourselves. Check the life support registration still stands, especially after a move or a change of retailer. Send the result to the Clinical Lead, who reviews it. A faulty backup is a serious fault: tell the treating team and the on-call manager the same day.

Result
The backup equipment works, servicing is up to date and the life support registration is current.
Record
FRM-HID-10 Q69 to Q71
Time limit
Every month. Confirm the registration at least every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 7Policy C7Written on: Form, question 69Form Q69Form, question 70Form Q70Form, question 71Form Q71

Step 29

The Service Manager

Arrange the treating team's review of the participant's ventilator health.

Check the participant still consents. Use Decision table 8 for an early review. Send the team the records they need, with consent. Support the participant to attend: transport, a worker who knows them and communication support. Ask the participant what they want to raise. After the review, enter the date, the changes and the next due date. If anything changed, repeat step 3 and step 30.

Result
The treating team has reviewed the participant, the plan is current and the next review date is set.
Record
FRM-HID-10 Q72 and Q73. REG-HID-02 High Intensity Supports Register
Time limit
At the interval the team sets, and no later than every 12 months. Ask within 1 business day of a trigger, and the same day for an urgent one (our standard)

Carries out: Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Written on: Form, question 72Form Q72Form, question 73Form Q73

Step 30

The Clinical Lead

Reassess each worker whose reassessment is due, before they next support the participant.

Reassess after any change to the device, the interface, the settings or the clinical content of the plan. A new review date or phone number does not lapse a sign-off. Reassess after an incident that suggests a gap, and when you think a worker cannot do a task. The trainer assesses on the participant's own equipment. A worker with a lapsed sign-off comes off the roster for this participant until they are signed off again.

Result
Every worker on the roster has a current sign-off.
Record
FRM-HID-10 Q74. FRM-HID-04 High Intensity Competency Assessment Record. REG-HID-01 High Intensity Training and Competency Register
Time limit
Every 12 months. Before the next shift after 3 months without supporting this participant, or after a change of settings, device or the clinical content of the plan (our standard, in line with the skills descriptor)

IfThen
You cannot reach the treating team's numberTry the after-hours number on the sheet. Then phone the on-call manager, who phones the Clinical Lead. Write down each time you tried. If the participant is getting worse, call 000
The plan on the sheet is out of date or missing, or does not match the plan at the bedsideChange nothing. Keep supporting the participant as the last signed plan says. Phone the Service Manager now. The Service Manager asks the treating team for the current plan the same day, and the Clinical Lead repeats step 3. If you think the participant's condition has changed, phone the treating team. Call 000 if they are unwell
No signed-off worker can come, or the only signed-off worker is ill, hurt or too tired to stay awakePhone the on-call manager at once. The on-call manager arranges a signed-off worker under PRO-COS-01 Continuity of Supports Procedure. An untrained worker never takes over a ventilator task and is never left alone with the participant. If nobody can come, the on-call manager phones the treating team for another safe arrangement. Call 000 if the participant is at risk
A worker you work with missed a check, was asleep, changed a setting or did a task they are not signed off forMake the participant safe first. Phone the on-call manager and write an incident report. Do not argue with the worker first. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The concern is about your manager, the Clinical Lead or the Chief ExecutivePhone the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, phone the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. You can always phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544
The participant says no to the treating team's review, or to sharing informationRespect it. Explain in their usual way of communicating what the review is for and what may happen without it. Offer an advocate and more time. Record their decision and the date at question 3. Tell the treating team only what the participant agrees to. If they still say no, the Clinical Lead and the Service Manager decide with them whether we can give the support safely, and record it. Ask again at each review
The participant refuses the ventilator, a task or a checkStay with them. Explain the risk in a way they understand. Offer another way if the plan allows one. Do not force them, and do not hold them or use any device. Respect a choice recorded on FRM-RGT-04 Dignity of Risk Decision Record. Phone the treating team the same day and tell the Service Manager. Call 000 if they are distressed or cannot breathe
A family member or visitor asks you to change a setting, or the participant's decision maker asks you toDo not change it. Say that only the treating team can. Offer to phone the team now. Tell the Service Manager. A family member who runs the machine does so under the team's training. We do not direct them
The ventilator, a battery or other equipment is faulty or damagedUse the backup as the plan says. Phone the supplier's technical support once the participant is safe. Tag the item as faulty and do not use it. If there is no working backup and the participant depends on the ventilator, call 000
A check was missed on an earlier shift, or the sheet or the form is missingDo the check now. Write what you found and that it was late. Tell the Service Manager and write an incident report. If the system is down, use a paper copy of FRM-HID-10. The Service Manager enters it within 1 business day of the system coming back
A deadline will be missed: a review, a sign-off, a service or the life support registrationTell the Clinical Lead before it passes. The Clinical Lead sets a new date, writes the reason at question 68 and enters it in REG-QMS-01. A worker's sign-off cannot be extended. The worker comes off the roster for this participant until they are reassessed
You cannot write the record because of an emergencyLook after the participant first. Write it before your shift ends. If you cannot, give it by phone to the on-call manager, who writes it in your words and reads it back
The participant cannot call for help, or the way they call has failedStay within sight until it works. Phone the Service Manager. Do not leave the participant alone. Write an incident report
You are not sure whether a reading, a sign or an alarm is seriousTreat it as serious. Phone the treating team's clinical number. If the participant looks unwell, call 000. Nobody is blamed for a call that turned out to be unneeded
The participant's wishes differ from the plan, or the participant and the treating team disagreeDo not change the plan. Tell the Service Manager. The Service Manager sets up a conversation between the participant and the team under PRO-RGT-04 Independence and Informed Choice Procedure, and records the outcome on FRM-RGT-04
The participant dies, or is seriously injuredCall 000 and stay with them. Phone the on-call manager at once. This is a reportable incident. The Quality Manager notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware, under PRO-INC-02 Reportable Incidents Notification Procedure
The home is not safe for the equipment, for example smoking near oxygen or no safe power pointTell the Service Manager at once. The Service Manager repeats FRM-ENV-01 and decides with the Clinical Lead whether supports go ahead. Remove the hazard yourself if you can do it safely
The treating team will not write or endorse a plan, or has not repliedWe do not start ventilator support. For a participant who cannot be off the ventilator, we give no shift-based support at all until a plan exists, because an untrained worker is never left alone with them. For a participant who uses the ventilator only at night or for part of the day, other agreed supports go ahead only while the participant is off the ventilator; workers never operate or check the ventilator, and call 000 in an emergency as for any participant. The Service Manager tells the participant, their support coordinator or the NDIA, and the people the participant chose, in the participant's usual way of communicating. The Service Manager phones the team's lead clinician, then asks the participant's doctor for a referral to another team. The Clinical Lead writes down each try
A worker is not confident to do a task, or you see a worker struggle with oneIf the participant is safe, stop the task. Another signed-off worker does it. Tell the Clinical Lead the same shift. The Clinical Lead decides whether the worker needs reassessing at step 30. Nobody is blamed for asking for help
We cannot meet a condition in the readiness checkWe do not start. The Service Manager tells the participant why, in their usual way of communicating, and says what is missing and when it could be ready. If we cannot ready it, the Service Manager follows PRO-SUP-01 Access to Supports Procedure to help the participant find another provider

8Done means

The ventilator support is set up when all of these are true:

  • the treating team's plan and prescription are on the ventilator sheet, and the team has checked the sheet
  • the participant has consented, and has told us how they call for help
  • every worker on the roster is signed off for this participant and this ventilator
  • the backup equipment, the power plan and the life support registration are in place
  • the readiness check at question 41 is signed.

Each shift is finished when all of these are true:

  • the start-of-shift checks, the observations and the care are recorded
  • every alarm, call and emergency is logged, and every incident report is written
  • the next worker has been told.

These records now exist:

  • FRM-HID-10 Ventilator Check and Care Record, kept in the participant's file
  • the participant's entry in REG-HID-02 High Intensity Supports Register: the plan, the consent, the treating team, the reviews and the next review due
  • a sign-off in FRM-HID-04 and a row in REG-HID-01 for each worker
  • FRM-INC-01 Incident Report Form and a row in REG-INC-01 Incident Register for each incident
  • an entry in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register for each action from the weekly check and the monthly read.

9Quick card

144 words
  • Look at the participant first, then the circuit, then the machine (step 19)
  • Blue or grey, struggling, not responding, or the machine cannot be fixed at once: call 000 and stay (step 20)
  • Signed off for it: start manual ventilation with the bag (step 21)
  • Machine failed: switch to the backup ventilator as the plan says (step 22)
  • Power cut: note the time, go to backup power, move by the move-by time (step 23)
  • Display must match the prescription. If it does not, change nothing and phone the treating team (step 13)
  • Never disable or mute an alarm. Stay within hearing, and awake unless the sheet says you may sleep (step 18)
  • Start of shift: check the display, the circuit, the backup and the power (step 12)
  • Before your shift ends: hand over and write an incident report if anything went wrong (step 25)

questions.hint: Give the full name, the participant number and every address where the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="ventilator" data-def="a machine that moves air into and out of a person's lungs, through a mask or through a tracheostomy. It includes bilevel and CPAP machines when workers help with them." data-source="POL-HID-07">ventilator</button> is used. Include day programs and vehicles.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: How did the participant take part in making their plan, and what do they want from their ventilator support?
questions.hint: Ask in their usual way of communicating. Write their own words. Say who helped, whether an advocate was offered and how long they had to decide.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: Does the participant agree to the treating team reviewing their ventilator support and health? Who gave that consent?
questions.hint: Write yes or no, the date and who consented. If someone else decides for them, write their name and the authority they hold. Attach FRM-INF-01.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: Who may we share the plan and these records with, in an emergency and at other times?
questions.hint: List each person or service: support network, other providers, the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="treating team" data-def="the respiratory doctor, home ventilation service or other health practitioners who prescribe the participant's ventilator and write or endorse their plan." data-source="POL-HID-07">treating team</button>, ambulance and hospital staff, government agencies. Say what each may see. Take this from FRM-INF-01.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: If someone else makes decisions for the participant, who is it, what authority do they hold, and how were the participant's own views still asked?
questions.hint: Sight the authority and check it covers health decisions. Write the name, the kind of authority, the date you saw it and how you asked the participant.
questions.optional: Yes, when the participant decides for themselves
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: How does the participant communicate, and how do they call for help while on the ventilator, by day and by night?
questions.hint: Describe the method: voice, switch, bell, eye gaze, board or device. Say where it sits, who tested it and when. Say how they show pain, fear or breathing trouble.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: Does the participant have an advance care directive? Where is it kept, and who has read it?
questions.hint: Write yes, no or not known. Give where the original and copies are. Give the name and date for each worker or manager who has read it. Every <button type="button" class="term" data-term="signed-off worker" data-def="a worker whom the trainer has signed off, task by task, for this participant and this ventilator, and whose sign-off is current." data-source="POL-HID-07">signed-off worker</button> reads it before their first shift. If there is none, say whether the participant was offered the chance to make one.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.text: What choices has the participant made about their ventilator support that workers must follow?
questions.hint: For example: the times they choose to be off it, the worker they prefer, how they like to be positioned, what they refuse. Attach FRM-RGT-04 for any choice that goes against the team's advice.
questions.optional: Yes, when the participant has made none
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 1Procedure step 1

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Who is the treating team, and how do we reach them in hours and after hours?
questions.hint: Give the service, and the name and role of the clinician who oversees the participant's ventilator. Give every phone number. Test each number and write the date.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 2Procedure step 2

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Who prescribed the settings, on what date, and which version of the treating team's plan is this?
questions.hint: Write the prescriber's name and role, the date on the prescription, and the date and version of the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="plan" data-def="the treating team's written plan and prescription for this participant. It may sit in FRM-HID-01 Participant Health Support Plan if the team has written or endorsed it there." data-source="POL-HID-07">plan</button>. If the team gave no date, ask. Do not guess.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 2Procedure step 2

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Which ventilator does the participant use, and who supplies and services it?
questions.hint: Write the make, model and serial number. Give the supplier's name and its technical support number. Say who holds the supplier contract: the participant, the treating team or us.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: What kind of ventilation does the participant have, and how dependent are they on it?
questions.hint: Choose mask, or both. Write the mode in the words the team uses. Choose the level of dependence the team writes. For a tracheostomy, PRO-HID-04 also applies.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: How long can the participant safely be off the ventilator?
questions.hint: Copy the time the team wrote, or the words 'must not be off'. If the team has not written it, write 'not written' and treat the participant as unable to be off it. Ask the team to write it.

controls.label: Time, or 'must not be off', or 'not written'

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: When is the ventilator used?
questions.hint: Write the hours of use. Write any breaks the plan allows, such as meals or outings.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: What mask or tracheostomy tube does the participant use?
questions.hint: Write the type, make and size. Write any fitting notes and cuff arrangements exactly as the team wrote them. List the spare.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: What are the prescribed settings?
questions.hint: One line per setting: the name as shown on the display, the value and the unit. Copy exactly. Never round or convert.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: What are the prescribed alarm limits?
questions.hint: One line per <button type="button" class="term" data-term="alarm" data-def="a sound or message on the ventilator that tells a worker something is wrong." data-source="POL-HID-07">alarm</button>: the name as shown on the display, then the low limit and the high limit. Copy exactly.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: How is the air humidified, and what water is used?
questions.hint: Write the humidifier or filter the team prescribes, the kind of water, and how and when to fill it, as the supplier's instructions say. Write 'none' if none.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Is oxygen prescribed, and if so, how?
questions.hint: Write 'none', or the flow or percentage the team prescribes, the source, when it is used and where the spare is kept. A signed-off worker turns it on and off at the prescribed flow only where the sheet says so, and never changes the flow. Write the fire safety rules for the home.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Which observations does the team want workers to take, how often, and what is the participant's own normal range for each?
questions.hint: One line per observation: name; how often; the range; what to do if the reading is outside it; who to call. Include only what the team asks for. Write the participant's <button type="button" class="term" data-term="own oxygen level" data-def="how much oxygen is in the participant's blood, usually measured with a probe on the finger. It is not the oxygen the ventilator delivers." data-source="POL-HID-07">own oxygen level</button> (saturation) apart from the oxygen the ventilator delivers.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: What does each alarm on this ventilator mean, and what is the first action for it?
questions.hint: One line per alarm: the name or sound; what it means for this participant; the first checks (the participant, then the circuit, then the machine); when to call the team; when to call 000.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Which tasks has the team included in the plan for signed-off workers?
questions.hint: Tick each that applies: fit or adjust the mask; suction; <button type="button" class="term" data-term="manual ventilation" data-def="moving air into the lungs by hand, with a resuscitation bag joined to the mask or the tracheostomy." data-source="POL-HID-07">manual ventilation</button> with a bag; switch to the backup ventilator; cough assist; cuff checks; other. Ticking a task does not sign off a worker. Sign-off is on FRM-HID-04.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Which parts must be cleaned or changed, how often, and when is each next due?
questions.hint: One line per part: mask or interface, tubing, filter, humidifier chamber, inner parts, other. Write how often as the team or the supplier says, the date last done and the date next due.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Has the team written steps for each emergency, and where are they?
questions.hint: For each, write yes or no and where the steps are: ventilator failure; power failure; disconnection; mask or circuit leak; blocked airway or tracheostomy; breathing distress; manual ventilation. Any no: ask the team before you go on.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: If the plan includes manual ventilation, when does a worker start it, and where is the bag kept?
questions.hint: Write when to start, the bag, the mask or adapter, and where they are kept, as the plan says. Write 'not in the plan' if it is not.
questions.optional: Yes, when the plan has no manual ventilation
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: How often will the team review the participant's ventilator support, what early-review triggers did they set, and who arranges the visit?
questions.hint: Write the interval in months, any triggers the team added to Decision table 8 in PRO-HID-06, the date of the last review and the date the next is due.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Has the participant been given the plan in a form they can use, and was it explained to them?
questions.hint: Say how you went through it in their usual way of communicating, who was there and the date. Say what form their copy is in, for example plain language, pictures, audio or large print, and where they keep it.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section B: The prescription and the plan
questions.text: Has the treating team checked this sheet against their own plan?
questions.hint: Write the name and role of the person who checked, the date and how: their signature, or their written confirmation by email. Where the treating team issues its own prescription sheet, attach it as Section B and record its version at Q10; the team's own sheet stands as checked, and the copies only the items it lacks. Do not use the sheet until this is done.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 3Procedure step 3

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: What backup equipment does this participant need, where is each item kept, and how long does it last?
questions.hint: One line per item: backup ventilator if the team requires one; external battery; manual ventilation bag with the right mask or adapter; portable suction; spare circuit and interface; spare oxygen; torch; other. Write where it is kept, the charge or amount, the run time and the date last tested.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 5Procedure step 5

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: How long does each battery run for this participant's settings, and what is the move-by time?
questions.hint: Write the run time of the internal battery and the external battery, and the source: the team or the supplier's instructions. Write the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="move-by time" data-def="how long before a battery runs out the participant must be on other power or moved. The treating team sets it." data-source="POL-HID-07">move-by time</button>: how long before a battery runs out the participant must be on other power or moved. The team sets it.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 5Procedure step 5

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: What do workers do in a power cut, and where does the participant go in a long outage?
questions.hint: Write the steps in order. Say where the participant goes, how they get there, who arranges it and who goes with them. Write the date of their personal emergency plan in FRM-SUP-02 and check it matches.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 5Procedure step 5

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: Is the participant registered as a life support customer with their electricity retailer and distributor?
questions.hint: Write yes or no for the retailer and for the distributor, the date the advice was given, the date the medical confirmation was returned, the reference number, the date last confirmed and the date next due. If the participant chose not to register, write that and the date. The medical confirmation is signed by a registered medical practitioner (the participant's doctor or the team's doctor) and returned within the retailer's deadline.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 6Procedure step 6

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: What is the staffing rule, using Decision table 1 in PRO-HID-06?
questions.hint: Write who must be awake, who must be within hearing, whether the participant may be alone and for how long, and how many workers go on outings. The signed-off worker is never the driver on an outing. If the team has not written how long the participant can be off, use the first row.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 4Procedure step 4

questions.section: Section C: Backup, power and staffing
questions.text: Who covers if the signed-off worker cannot come?
questions.hint: Name at least one other signed-off worker. Say who phones them and when. Say what happens if none can come: the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="on-call manager" data-def="the manager who takes workers' calls. In office hours this is the Service Manager. After hours it is the rostered manager. A clinical question goes to the treating team's clinical number, or to the Clinical Lead." data-source="POL-HID-07">on-call manager</button>, family, the treating team. An untrained worker is never the answer.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 4Procedure step 4

questions.text: Is ventilator management on our certificate of registration?
questions.hint: Check the certificate. Write yes or no and the date you checked. If no, we do not start.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Who is the Clinical Lead for this participant?
questions.hint: Name the registered nurse, or other health practitioner whose scope covers the support, whom we engage to oversee our ventilator support, and say where REG-GOV-01 names them. A sole trader names an outside practitioner.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Is there a training plan for this participant's workers, and who delivers each part?
questions.hint: Attach FRM-HID-03. The Clinical Lead sets the plan. Name each <button type="button" class="term" data-term="trainer" data-def="a health practitioner, or a person who meets the NDIS Commission skills descriptor for ventilator support, who trains and signs off workers." data-source="POL-HID-07">trainer</button> and their qualification. A health practitioner, or a person who meets the skills descriptor for ventilator support, delivers the training.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 7Procedure step 7Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: How many workers are signed off for this participant and this ventilator, and do they cover every ventilated shift for the next 4 weeks?
questions.hint: Count from REG-HID-01. Write the number, the date you checked and yes or no. Cover means one signed-off worker on every shift, plus a named backup.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Does every signed-off worker hold current CPR, and have they practised manual ventilation?
questions.hint: Check REG-HRM-02 for the CPR date. Check FRM-HID-04 for the manual ventilation sign-off, which every signed-off worker must hold. Write the dates. A worker with an expired date is off the roster.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Has each place the participant is ventilated been checked for safety?
questions.hint: Attach FRM-ENV-01. It must cover power points, space for equipment, safe oxygen storage, no smoking or flames near oxygen, a place for backup power, and whether the alarm can be heard from where the worker will be. For a vehicle, check the machine is secured, the power outlet works, the battery covers the trip and oxygen is stowed safely; the outing check at Q63 records each trip.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Is everything in Sections A to D done, and may the support start?
questions.hint: Every answer must be yes. Write the date supports may start. The Clinical Lead and the Service Manager both sign. One no means no start: write what is missing, who fixes it and by when.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 9Procedure step 9

questions.text: Who is on shift, and when does the shift start and end?
questions.hint: Write your full name, your initials, your role, and the date and times. Sign it. Your initials on any other entry lead back to this line. Say whether you are signed off for this participant and this ventilator, with the date of your sign-off.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 10Procedure step 10

questions.text: Have you read the ventilator sheet and the last handover, and does the sheet's plan date match the plan at the bedside?
questions.hint: Write the plan date on the sheet and the date on the bedside plan. If they differ, do not change anything. Phone the Service Manager.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 10Procedure step 10

questions.text: How is the participant at the start of the shift?
questions.hint: Write what they tell you in their own words. Write what you see: colour, breathing, comfort, alertness. Write 'as usual' only if it is.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 11Procedure step 11

questions.text: Does the participant's way of calling for help work, and is it within their reach?
questions.hint: Test it now. Write the method, the time you tested it and yes or no. If it does not work, fix it before you do anything else.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 11Procedure step 11

questions.text: For the mode, each prescribed setting and each alarm limit, what does the display show?
questions.hint: One line per item on the sheet: name; prescribed value; value on the display; match yes or no. Never change a setting.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 12Procedure step 12

questions.text: Do the mode, every setting and every alarm limit match the prescription?
questions.hint: Yes only if every line matches. If any line is no, answer the next question.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 12Procedure step 12

questions.text: If anything did not match, who did you phone, when, and what did they tell you to do?
questions.hint: Write the name, the number, the time and the instruction. You never change a setting yourself.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 13Procedure step 13

questions.text: Are the alarms on at the volume the plan sets, and not silenced? Is the control lock on, if the team set it?
questions.hint: Write yes or no for each. If the participant has a remote alarm, test it and write the result. Never disable, mute or turn an alarm below the volume the plan sets.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 12Procedure step 12

questions.text: What did you find when you checked the interface, circuit and humidifier?
questions.hint: One line per item: mask seal and fit or tracheostomy connection; tubing; filter; humidifier water level and kind; skin under the mask or around the stoma; spare circuit and interface. Write okay, or what you found and did.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 14Procedure step 14

questions.text: For each item on the backup list in Section C, is it present, in place, charged or full, and working?
questions.hint: One line per item, including spare circuits, filters, masks and suction catheters. Write yes or no, and anything missing or low. Tell the on-call manager about any no before the outgoing worker leaves. Tell the Service Manager about any shortage of spares.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 15Procedure step 15

questions.text: What is the power position?
questions.hint: Write whether mains power is on, the internal battery charge, the external battery charge and the run time left from the sheet. Write the ventilator's usage-hours counter where it shows one. Write any planned outage you know of today.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 15Procedure step 15

questions.text: If oxygen is prescribed, what flow is the equipment delivering, and how much supply is left?
questions.hint: Write the flow or percentage the equipment shows, and the prescribed one. This is not the participant's own oxygen level. Write that in the observations.
questions.optional: Yes, when no oxygen is prescribed
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 15Procedure step 15

questions.text: What observations did you take?
questions.hint: One line per reading: time; name; the participant's own range from the sheet; the value; inside or outside; what you did. Take only what the sheet asks for. The participant's own oxygen level goes here. The oxygen delivered goes in the start-of-shift check.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 16Procedure step 16

questions.text: When was the participant on and off the ventilator?
questions.hint: Write the time on and the time off. For any time off that the sheet does not allow, write why (the participant's choice, the team's advice or an equipment problem) and who agreed.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 17Procedure step 17

questions.text: Which care tasks did you do, and at what time?
questions.hint: One line per task the sheet sets for this shift: mask or interface care; skin check; humidifier; cleaning; positioning; any other task the plan names for a signed-off worker, such as cough assist or a cuff check, with the time and any reading. Write done or not done, the time, and why if not done. Never do a task you are not signed off for.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 17Procedure step 17

questions.text: Which parts were due to be changed or cleaned this shift, and were they?
questions.hint: Check the schedule on the sheet. One line per part: due date; done date. Write the next due date.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 17Procedure step 17

questions.text: What alarms sounded?
questions.hint: One line per alarm: time; alarm name; how the participant was; what you found in the person, the circuit and the machine; what you did; cleared yes or no; who you phoned. Write 'none' if none.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 19Procedure step 19

questions.text: Was a signed-off worker awake and within hearing of the alarm the whole time the participant was on the ventilator?
questions.hint: Answer yes or no. If no, write from when to when, why, and who you told. A no needs an <button type="button" class="term" data-term="incident" data-def="has the meaning in POL-INC-01 Incident Management Policy." data-source="POL-HID-07">incident</button> report.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 18Procedure step 18

questions.text: Was there an emergency?
questions.hint: Write 'none', or: the time it began; what you saw; the time you called 000; whether you started manual ventilation or CPR, and when; whether you switched to the backup ventilator; who took over; how the participant was after.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 20Procedure step 20Procedure, step 21Procedure step 21Procedure, step 22Procedure step 22

questions.text: Who did you phone this shift about the participant's ventilator, and what happened?
questions.hint: One line per call: who (treating team, on-call manager, supplier, 000); time; why; what they advised; what you did.
questions.optional: Yes, when you made no calls
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 16Procedure step 16Procedure, step 20Procedure step 20Procedure, step 22Procedure step 22

questions.text: Did anything need an incident report, and what is its number?
questions.hint: Write yes or no. These need one: an alarm you could not clear; a failure; a power cut; a disconnection with harm; a call to 000; a missed check; a mismatch; a worker without a sign-off. Near misses count. Write the FRM-INC-01 number.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 26Procedure step 26

questions.section: Section G: Outings and power cuts
questions.text: Before an outing: did you complete the outing check?
questions.hint: Write the date, the place and how long you will be away. Write the portable battery run time from the sheet, the margin the plan sets and the charge when you left. Write yes or no for: spare interface and circuit; suction; bag and mask; oxygen and supply; the sheet and numbers; vehicle power. Write who goes.
questions.optional: Yes, when there was no outing
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 24Procedure step 24

questions.section: Section G: Outings and power cuts
questions.text: After the outing: how did it go?
questions.hint: Write the time back, any alarm or problem, the battery charge on return, and whether everything is recharged.
questions.optional: Yes, when there was no outing
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 24Procedure step 24

questions.section: Section G: Outings and power cuts
questions.text: If the power failed, what happened?
questions.hint: Write the time it failed; what the ventilator switched to; the time backup power started; the move-by time; who you told and when; the time power returned or the participant moved; where they went; how they were.
questions.optional: Yes, when the power did not fail
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 23Procedure step 23

questions.text: What does the next worker need to know?
questions.hint: Write the participant's position, the total time on the ventilator, how they are communicating today, parts due, any equipment fault and anything you watched. Tell the next worker in person. Do not leave a participant who cannot be off the ventilator until a signed-off worker has taken over in person; if nobody comes, phone the on-call manager.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 25Procedure step 25

questions.text: Is the plan not meeting the participant's needs, or does the participant want a change?
questions.hint: Write what you saw or heard, in the participant's words where you can. This goes to the Clinical Lead and may start an early review. Write 'none' if none.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 25Procedure step 25

questions.text: What did the weekly completeness check and the monthly sample read show?
questions.hint: Service Manager, every week: write the date and your name, and each blank, missed check, 'no' at the hearing question and missed due date. Clinical Lead, every month and after any incident or plan change: list each mismatch, alarm pattern and power cut. Write each action, its owner and due date, and enter each in REG-QMS-01. Write what you sent to the treating team.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 27Procedure step 27

questions.text: What did the monthly equipment test show?
questions.hint: Write the date and who tested: the Service Manager, or the senior signed-off worker named for it. Test the backup ventilator, the batteries and any generator with the supplier's checklist and as the supplier's instructions say. Write the result, any fault and the action, and the date the Clinical Lead reviewed it. A faulty backup is a serious fault: tell the treating team.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 28Procedure step 28

questions.text: Which servicing is due, and is any overdue?
questions.hint: One line per item: item; how often and whose instructions; last service; next due; who does it. Write any overdue service and what you did. We never service a ventilator ourselves.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 28Procedure step 28

questions.text: Is the life support registration still current?
questions.hint: Check with the participant and the retailer. Write the date, who checked, yes or no, and any change: a move, a new retailer, a new meter. Check at least every 12 months and after any move.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 28Procedure step 28

questions.text: When did the treating team last review the participant, and what changed?
questions.hint: Write the date, the practitioner, what changed (settings, plan, device or hours), the new plan version, the date the next review is due and whether the participant's consent is still current. Write what the participant asked for or said. Attach the team's signature or written confirmation.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 29Procedure step 29

questions.text: Has anything happened that needs an early review, and has it been asked for?
questions.hint: Use Decision table 8 in PRO-HID-06. Write what happened, the date, the date you asked, and the date it was held. Write 'none' if none.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure, step 29Procedure step 29

questions.text: Has anything changed that needs workers to be reassessed?
questions.hint: Write what changed (device, settings, interface, the clinical content of the plan, or 3 months without support), the date workers were told, and the names of workers re-signed off before their next shift. Check FRM-HID-04.

form.intro:
This record holds what a worker and a manager write down about one participant's ventilator support: the plan, the checks, the care, the alarms and the reviews. Keep one record for each participant who uses a ventilator. PRO-HID-06 Ventilator Management Procedure says when to complete each part.

Who completes it, and when:

  • Sections A and D: the Service Manager, before the first shift.
  • Section B: the Clinical Lead, before the first shift, from the treating team's own documents. Where the treating team issues its own prescription sheet, attach it as Section B and record its version at Q10; the Clinical Lead copies only the items it lacks.
  • Section C: the Service Manager and the Clinical Lead, before the first shift.
  • Sections B and C are the ventilator sheet. Keep a printed copy at the bedside, with Decision tables 5 and 7 of PRO-HID-06.
  • Sections E, F and H: the signed-off worker, on every shift.
  • Section G: the signed-off worker, when there is an outing or a power cut.
  • Section I: the Service Manager every week and every month; the Clinical Lead every month, after any incident or plan change, and at each review.

Have ready: the treating team's plan and prescription, the participant's consent record (FRM-INF-01), the supplier's instructions for the ventilator, and REG-HID-01 High Intensity Training and Competency Register.

Rules for the record:

  • Write in ink, or use an electronic record that locks each entry. Rule one line through a mistake, initial it and write the right entry beside it. Never erase it.
  • Copy the plan word for word. Never fill a gap. Ask the treating team.
  • Never change a setting. Never write a value you did not read or take.
  • If you do not know an answer during the shift, write 'not known' and phone the on-call manager. Never guess.

Every page of the record carries these lines:

  • Blue or grey, struggling to breathe, not responding, or the ventilator cannot be made to work: call 000 now and stay with the participant.
  • The display does not match the prescription: change nothing. Phone the treating team's clinical number on the sheet.
  • An alarm: look at the participant first, then the circuit, then the machine.
  • A power cut: note the time and go to backup power. Move the participant by the move-by time.
  • An alarm you could not clear, a failure, a power cut or a call to 000: write an incident report (FRM-INC-01) before your shift ends.

What happens next: the Service Manager checks every shift record for completeness each week. The Clinical Lead reads a sample every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change. The Service Manager enters the plan, consent, treating team and review dates in REG-HID-02 High Intensity Supports Register. Full pages go into the participant's file.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to give safe ventilator support, to show that each check was done, and to meet our legal duties under the NDIS Act 2013 and the Practice Standards.

The signed-off workers, the Clinical Lead, the Service Manager and the Quality Manager read it. With the participant's consent we share it with the treating team, the equipment supplier and other health services. In an emergency we give it to ambulance and hospital staff where the law allows. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form records the consent.

If you are the participant, you can ask to see your record and ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
• Signed-off worker: keep the current page at the bedside for the whole shift. Complete Section H and phone the on-call manager about any call or incident before your shift ends (our standard).
  • Signed-off worker: write an incident report (FRM-INC-01) for anything on the list at question 62 before your shift ends (our standard).
  • Clinical Lead: read a sample of the record every month, and every record after an incident or a plan change, and complete Q68 (our standard).
  • Service Manager: check the record for completeness every week and complete Q68 within 7 days of the last entry. Run the monthly equipment test and complete Q69 (our standard).
  • Service Manager: enter any change to the plan, the consent, the treating team or the review dates in REG-HID-02 within 2 (our standard).
  • Quality Manager: sample the records in the internal audit set by POL-HID-07 Ventilator Management Policy.
  • Service Manager: file each full page in the participant's file within 7 days of its last entry (our standard).
  • Keep each page for 7 years after its last entry (statutory: NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026: records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years). The health records law of [state or territory] can require longer, and so can a record about a child.
  • A page that records an incident is kept with the incident record for 7 years (statutory: Incident Management and Reportable Incidents Rules, section 12(4), and section 25(2) for a reportable incident).
